           The rest of the paper is organized as follows. In Section 2, we review some preliminaries on the
       local height pairing. In Section 3, we state and prove the main theorem 3.23. In Section 4, we
       consider the case of good reduction in detail. In Section 5, we reflect on the utility of Muse Spark

                                        2. Preliminaries on local height

           In this section, we fix conventions for the N´eron–Tate local height pairing and for regular
       semistable models.

           For an abelian group A, we denote by AR the R-vector space A ⊗Z R. In particular, we restrict
       to curves with semistable reduction. Hence, the special fiber of a regular integral model is reduced,
       and no multiplicities of irreducible components occur.

       2.1. Non-Archimedean setup and semistable models. Let K be a non-Archimedean local
       field. Let O be its valuation ring, let m = (π) be the maximal ideal with uniformizer π, let F = O/m
       be the residue field of characteristic p, and let q = |F| (a power of p). We fix the normalized valuation
       vK : K× → Z with vK(π) = 1 and the normalized absolute value |π|K = q−1. We write log for the
       natural logarithm; all formulas are homogeneous in the choice of log q, and we set log |π|−1 K = log q.

           For the remainder of Section 2, let X be a smooth, projective, geometrically connected curve
       over K of genus g ≥ 1.1

       Definition 2.1. Let Y be a scheme. By a divisor on Y, we mean a Cartier divisor on Y . We
       denote the group of Cartier divisors on Y by Div(Y ), and its degree zero subgroup by Div0(Y ).

           1For g = 0, the integral model defined below might not be unique. However, our results should still hold in this
